_about: Rule table for 'This week's air and your health' (backend/weekly.py). Every text is hedged and cites sources [n] listed in docs/health_advisory_reference.md (exact quotes in section 8). levels: clean (no valid day with AQI >= 101), episode (1-3 such days), persistent (>= 4 of 7). min_category: the worst valid day of the week must be at least this CPCB category (min_category_healthy: a stricter level for healthy adults). groups: lung, heart, child, older, pregnant, outdoor_work (outdoor workers), exercise (regular outdoor exercisers), healthy, or all. A group is named only where the source names it. long_term items are shown ONLY for persistent weeks. text: **...** marks phrases shown in bold (presentation only; weekly.py strips the markers into 'text' and keeps 'marked').

clean.text: Good news: **no day this week reached Moderate or worse** on the CPCB AQI scale.
clean.basis: CPCB category bands [1]; our daily AQI

clean.text: At Good and Satisfactory levels **no special precautions are needed** for the general population.
At Satisfactory levels, air may cause **minor breathing discomfort** to sensitive people.
clean.basis: [1] CPCB report Table 3.12 'Health Statements for AQI Categories' (printed p. 36): 'Satisfactory (51–100) May cause minor breathing discomfort to sensitive people'; [2] Arthapedia AQI table: 'Satisfactory (51–100) May cause minor breathing discomfort to sensitive people.'; [3] ASHA handbook 2024 p. 31 table, Satisfactory: 'May cause: Minor breathing discomfort in vulnerable populations'

short_term.text: On polluted days, short-term exposure may cause **headache, giddiness, eye irritation, coughing or breathlessness**.
short_term.basis: [4] HAP 2021 p. 41 poster 'Short term effects: Headache, Giddiness; Irritation in eyes; Coughing; Breathlessness; Skin Irritation'. Shown to vulnerable groups from Moderate, to healthy adults only from Poor (design, following the category impacts: Moderate 'Breathing or other health discomforts in vulnerable populations', Poor 'Breathing discomfort in healthy people' [3] p. 31; CPCB Moderate names sensitive groups [2])

short_term.text: People with lung disease such as asthma or COPD are **at higher risk**: Moderate air may cause them breathing discomfort, and Moderate to Poor air is linked to asthma attacks and acute respiratory illness.
short_term.basis: [1] Moderate 'breathing discomfort to the people with lung disease such as asthma'; [2] Moderate 'breathing discomfort to people with lung disease such as asthma'; [4] p. 25 Moderate to Poor 'Acute Respiratory Illnesses ... Asthma exacerbation'

short_term.text: People with heart disease are **at higher risk**: Moderate to Poor air may cause them discomfort and is linked to heart problems such as acute coronary syndrome.
short_term.basis: [1][2] Moderate and Poor impact 'discomfort to people with heart disease'; [4] p. 25 'Cardiovascular problems- Acute Coronary Syndrome'

short_term.text: Children are **among the groups at higher risk**: WHO counts air pollution among the greatest environmental risks to child health, and Moderate air may cause discomfort to children.
short_term.basis: [7] key fact 'Air pollution is one of the greatest environmental risks to child health'; [1][2] Moderate impact names children

short_term.text: Older adults are **among the groups at higher risk**: Moderate air may cause discomfort to older adults.
short_term.basis: [1][2] Moderate impact names older adults; [4] p. vii 'the elderly ... more vulnerable'

short_term.text: Pregnant women are among the groups **more vulnerable to air pollution**.
short_term.basis: [4] p. vii 'pregnant women ... are more vulnerable to air pollution'; [5] 'Children & Pregnant women'

short_term.text: Outdoor workers and people who exercise outdoors are among the groups **more vulnerable to air pollution**.
short_term.basis: [4] p. vii 'outdoor workers ... and athletes are more vulnerable'; [5] 'Outdoor workers'

short_term.text: Poor air may cause **breathing discomfort even in healthy people** on prolonged exposure.
short_term.basis: [1][2] Poor 'breathing discomfort to people on prolonged exposure'; [3] Poor 'Breathing discomfort in healthy people'

short_term.text: Very Poor air may cause **respiratory illness on prolonged exposure**, with effects more pronounced in people with lung and heart disease.
This week's main pollutant was PM2.5: fine particles that can **penetrate the lung barrier and enter the blood system**.
short_term.basis: [6] '... (≤ PM2.5 ...) can penetrate the lung barrier and enter the blood system'

short_term.text: This week's main pollutant was PM10: particles that can penetrate and **lodge deep inside the lungs**, which can cause irritation and inflammation.
short_term.basis: [6] '(≤ PM10) can penetrate and lodge deep inside the lungs, causing irritation, inflammation ...'

short_term.text: This week's main pollutant was ground-level ozone, which WHO calls a major factor in **causing asthma or making it worse**.
short_term.basis: [6] 'Ozone is a major factor in causing asthma (or making it worse)'

long_term.text: Sustained exposure over months and years is linked to **heart disease, stroke, chronic lung disease such as COPD, and lung cancer**.
long_term.basis: [7] deaths 'due to ischaemic heart disease and stroke ... chronic obstructive pulmonary disease ... lung cancers'; [8] executive summary p. 1 'Air pollution increases morbidity and mortality from cardiovascular and respiratory disease and from lung cancer'; [4] p. 41 long-term effects

long_term.text: Long-term exposure is linked to the development and worsening of **chronic respiratory diseases such as asthma and COPD**.
long_term.basis: [4] p. 6 Table 2, long-term 'Chronic respiratory diseases incidence & prevalence (asthma, COPD, chronic pathological changes)'

long_term.text: Long-term exposure is linked to **chronic cardiovascular disease**, including heart attack.
long_term.basis: [4] p. 6 'Chronic cardiovascular diseases'; p. 41 'Cardiovascular Diseases (Heart Attack)'

long_term.text: Sustained exposure during pregnancy is linked to **restricted growth of the baby before birth** (low birth weight).
long_term.basis: [4] p. 6 long-term 'Intrauterine growth restrictions (low birth weight at term, intrauterine growth retardation, small for gestational age)'

actions.text: On Moderate days, **reduce prolonged or strenuous outdoor physical exertion**.
On Moderate days, **avoid prolonged or strenuous outdoor physical exertion**.
On Poor days, **avoid outdoor physical activities**.
On Poor days, **avoid outdoor physical exertion**.
On Very Poor or Severe days, **remain indoors and keep activity levels low**.
**Plan outdoor activity for cleaner hours** (see 'Usually cleanest at this station'); WHO advises adapting the timing and location of physical activity to reduce exposure.
actions.basis: [5] 'adapt the timing and location of physical activity to reduce exposure'

actions.text: **Keep your prescribed medicines readily available** and follow your doctor's instructions.
actions.basis: [4] p. 39 'Persons with airway, lung or heart illnesses should keep their medications readily available'; p. 44 'Properly follow personal doctor's instructions'

actions.text: **Keep doors and windows closed** in the early morning and late evening; ventilate in the afternoon (12 to 4 pm).
**Avoid going to places with heavy traffic** and congested areas.
If you work outdoors, **take frequent water breaks** between work.
actions.basis: [3] ASHA handbook 2024 p. 31, Chapter 03 table 'AQI Levels, Health Effects and Protective Health Measures' (air pollution, not heat advice), Moderate, Messages for Vulnerable Population: 'Ensure taking frequent water breaks between work'; Poor, general population: 'Take frequent water breaks between work'

actions.text: On Very Poor or Severe days use a **close-fitted N95 or N99 mask** while going out. WHO cautions that no one respirator can be guaranteed to fit all users, and that people with lung or heart disease need **special caution**.
There are **no commercial respirators designed for children** (based on information available as of February 2019); **keep children indoors** with low activity on Very Poor or Severe days.
actions.basis: [5] question 'Can respirators protect from air pollution in the occupational setting?': 'There are no commercial respirators designed for children (based on information available as of February 2019)'; [4] vulnerable population 'Remain indoors and keep activity levels low'

actions.text: **Use clean smokeless fuels** (gas or electricity) for cooking and heating, and don't burn wood, leaves or garbage.
**Consult the nearest doctor** if you have breathlessness, giddiness, cough, chest discomfort or pain, or red or watery eyes.
actions.basis: [4] pp. 39, 44 'Consult the nearest doctor in case of breathlessness, giddiness, cough, chest discomfort or pain, irritation in the eyes (red or watery)'

notes.who: WHO 24-hour guideline levels are set at the 99th percentile, i.e. about 3-4 days a year above the level are expected even where the guideline is met [8].
notes.india: India's 24-hour (and 8-hour) limits must be met 98% of the time in a year; they may be exceeded on 2% of days, but not on two consecutive days [9].
